reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Commission creation, membership, terms, and vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1959 H.B. 266 §§ 2, 3 through A.L. 1998 S.B. 786). Covers creation of the eleven-member Missouri Commission on Human Rights, congressional-district representation, unpaid service, gubernatorial appointment with senate advice and consent, chairperson designation, six-year terms, six-member party cap, and filling unexpired terms after death or resignation.

headings.title: Commission purpose and general antidiscrimination function
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Describes the commission's general function to encourage fair treatment, foster mutual understanding and respect, and discourage discrimination against chapter-protected groups, their members, and persons with disabilities, distinct from its formal powers in section 213.030. Separate review: Revised during review from "Commission purpose and educational functions" because the statutory text describes encouraging fair treatment, fostering mutual understanding and respect, and discouraging discrimination without using the term "educational".

headings.title: Pre-1986 local commissions and section 213.135 limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes, including the 1990 Yellow Freight Systems case annotation (791 S.W.2d 382) stating subsection 3 does not empower local governments to create causes of action or determine violations and awards. Covers local commissions established prior to August 13, 1986, substantial-equivalency certification, and limiting administrative proceedings and remedies solely to section 213.135.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and all notes (L. 1959 H.B. 266 §§ 2, 3 through A.L. 1998 S.B. 786), including the 1990 Yellow Freight Systems, Inc. v. Mayor's Commission on Human Rights of the City of Springfield annotation (791 S.W.2d 382), and verified all fingerprints. Checked eleven-member commission appointment/party-cap rules, August 13, 1986 cutoff and section 213.135 limitation for local commissions, and Yellow Freight caveat on local ordinance causes of action. Revised subsection 2 title to remove unstated "educational"; retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: Enumerated powers and duties of the commission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (14)) and notes, including the 1998 Gerlach annotation (980 S.W.2d 589) on investigatory subpoenas duces tecum. Covers jurisdiction, conciliation, policies, staffing, agency services, rulemaking, complaint handling, hearings and subpoenas, publications, annual reports, official seal, federal/local work-sharing, grants/gifts, and establishing the human rights fund.

headings.title: Rulemaking effectiveness under section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Conditions effectiveness of any rule or portion of a rule promulgated under chapter 213 on promulgation pursuant to section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including subsection 1 subdivisions (1) to (14)) and all notes (L. 1959 H.B. 266 § 4 through A.L. 1998 S.B. 786), including the 1998 Gerlach v. Missouri Commission on Human Rights annotation (980 S.W.2d 589) on investigatory subpoenas duces tecum, and verified all fingerprints. Checked enumerated commission powers, section 213.010 human rights fund authority, and section 536.024 rulemaking effectiveness rule. Both titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Prohibited housing discrimination practices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (7), including paragraphs (a) to (c) of (6) and (7)) and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43). Lists unlawful housing practices in sales, rentals, terms, services, advertising, availability representations, blockbusting, and disability discrimination affecting buyers, renters, residents, or associated persons.

headings.title: Disability modifications, accommodations, and multifamily design
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1) to (3) and subparagraphs a. to d.) and history note. Defines disability discrimination for sections 213.040, 213.045, and 213.050 to include refusal of tenant-paid reasonable modifications (with landlord restoration conditions), refusal of reasonable accommodations, and failure to meet accessibility and adaptive-design standards for covered multifamily dwellings for first occupancy after March 13, 1991.

headings.title: Meaning of covered multifamily dwelling
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note. Defines 'covered multifamily dwelling' for subsection 2(3) as buildings of four or more units with one or more elevators, and ground-floor units in other four-or-more-unit buildings.

headings.title: ANSI A117.1 compliance for subsection 2(3)(a)
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. States that compliance with appropriate ANSI A117.1 accessibility requirements suffices specifically for paragraph (a) of subdivision (3) of subsection 2 (public and common use portions), not all of subdivision (3).

headings.title: Local design-code compliance and commission role
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 (subdivisions (1) to (3)) and history note. Treats compliance with local laws incorporating subsection 2(3) standards as satisfying that subdivision, authorizes local plan review, directs commission encouragement and technical assistance without mandating local review procedures, and disclaims any requirement that the commission review or approve all covered dwellings.

headings.title: Laws requiring greater disability accessibility preserved
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Preserves state, political subdivision, or other applicable laws requiring greater housing accessibility for persons with disabilities than chapter 213.

headings.title: Direct-threat and substantial-property-damage exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Clarifies that sections 213.040, 213.045, and 213.050 do not require making a dwelling available to a person whose tenancy poses a direct threat to others' health or safety or would cause substantial physical damage to others' property.

headings.title: Occupancy limits and older-persons housing exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Preserves reasonable local or state maximum-occupancy restrictions and exempts housing for older persons from familial-status provisions in sections 213.040, 213.045, and 213.050.

headings.title: Meaning of housing for older persons
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 (subdivisions (1) to (3) and paragraphs (a) to (c)) and history note. Defines 'housing for older persons' for sections 213.040, 213.045, and 213.050 across qualifying state/federal elderly programs, 62-and-older housing, and 55-and-older housing subject to commission regulations on facilities/services, 80-percent occupancy, and published policies.

headings.title: August 28, 1992 occupants and reserved unoccupied units
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 (subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note. Prevents loss of older-persons housing status due to non-age-qualifying residents living there as of August 28, 1992 (if new occupants qualify) or unoccupied units reserved for age-qualifying persons. Separate review: Revised during review from "Existing pre-1992 occupants and reserved unoccupied units" to preserve the exact statutory cutoff date ("as of August 28, 1992") rather than implying only pre-1992 residents.

headings.title: Exception for controlled-substance manufacture or distribution convictions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Clarifies that sections 213.040, 213.045, and 213.050 do not prohibit conduct against a person convicted of illegal manufacture or distribution of a controlled substance as defined in section 195.010.

headings.title: Exemptions for religious organizations and private clubs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history note. Permits religious organizations and affiliated nonprofits to limit noncommercial housing to co-religionists (unless membership is restricted by race, color, or national origin) and permits private clubs not open to the public to limit incidental noncommercial lodging to members.

headings.title: Exemptions for qualifying single-family and owner-occupied dwellings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 (subdivisions (1) and (2), including paragraphs (a) and (b)) and history note. Exempts qualifying private single-family house sales/rentals (subject to three-house, non-broker/no-advertisement, and 24-month non-resident sale limits) and owner-occupied dwellings of up to four families, while preserving subsection 1(3) discriminatory-advertising prohibitions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 13 subsections (including all subdivisions, paragraphs, and subparagraphs) and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43) and verified all fingerprints. Checked March 13, 1991 multifamily design date, narrow ANSI A117.1 scope limited to subsection 2(3)(a), local code review, direct-threat/occupancy/older-persons/controlled-substance/religious/private-club exceptions, and single-family/owner-occupied exemptions preserving subsection 1(3) advertising prohibitions. Revised subsection 10 title to preserve the exact August 28, 1992 resident cutoff date; retained other 12 titles.

headings.title: Prohibition on discriminatory homeowners' association covenants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 2005 S.B. 168, effective 1-01-06). Bars declarations and other governing documents of homeowners' associations from including restrictive covenants violating section 213.040.

headings.title: Board amendment and restatement without owner approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs a homeowners' association board of directors, notwithstanding other laws or governing documents and without owner approval, to amend and restate governing documents solely to remove a section 213.040-violating restrictive covenant.

headings.title: Notice to delete, injunctive enforcement, and attorney fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Authorizes the commission, a city or county where the development is located, or any person to sue for injunctive relief if an association fails to delete a violative covenant within thirty days after written notice, with discretionary attorney fees for the prevailing party.

headings.title: Effective date of section
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes (including 'Effective 1-01-06'). States that section 213.041 becomes effective on January 1, 2006.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and history/effective-date notes (L. 2005 S.B. 168; effective 1-01-06) and verified all fingerprints. Checked homeowners' association covenant ban, board amendment/restatement without owner approval, 30-day written-notice prerequisite for injunctive suits and permissive prevailing-party attorney fees, and January 1, 2006 effective date. All 4 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Prohibited employment practices by employers, unions, and agencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (3) and paragraphs (a) and (b)) and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43). Lists unlawful employment practices for employers, labor organizations, apprenticeship or training committees, and employment agencies, including the bona fide occupational qualification exception for job postings and inquiries.

headings.title: Bona fide seniority, merit, production, location, and ability-test exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Exempts nondiscriminatory seniority, merit, production-based, and work-location differences and professionally developed ability tests when not designed, intended, or used to discriminate.

headings.title: No requirement of preferential treatment for workforce imbalance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. States that chapter 213 does not require employers, employment agencies, labor organizations, or joint training committees to grant preferential treatment based on demographic imbalances in employment, referral, membership, or training.

headings.title: Compliance with 29 U.S.C. 623 for firefighters and officers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Exempts state and political subdivision compliance with 29 U.S.C. Section 623 relating to employment as firefighters or law enforcement officers from unlawful employment practice liability under chapter 213.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections (including subsection 1 subdivisions (1) to (3) and paragraphs (a)–(b)) and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43) and verified all fingerprints. Checked covered entities (employers, labor organizations, joint training committees, employment agencies), BFOQ exception, bona fide seniority/merit/production/location/ability-test exceptions, anti-preference clause, and state/local 29 U.S.C. 623 compliance for firefighters and officers. All 4 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Right to equal use of public accommodations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1986 S.B. 513 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43), including the 2012 Doe ex rel. Subia annotation (372 S.W.3d 43) on public-school student-on-student harassment claims. Declares entitlement to full and equal use and enjoyment of places of public accommodation without discrimination or segregation; note archived text says 'as hereinafter defined' while the definition appears in section 213.010.

headings.title: Prohibited denial or segregation in public accommodations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Declares it an unlawful discriminatory practice to directly or indirectly refuse, withhold, deny, attempt to deny, segregate, or discriminate in accommodations, advantages, facilities, services, or privileges of a place of public accommodation as defined in section 213.010 and this section.

headings.title: Exemptions for private clubs and nonpublic religious places
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Exempts private clubs, places owned or operated on behalf of religious corporations, associations, or societies, and other establishments not open to the public, unless their facilities are made available to patrons of a place of public accommodation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and all notes (L. 1986 S.B. 513 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43), including the 2012 Doe ex rel. Subia v. Kansas City, Missouri School District annotation (372 S.W.3d 43) on public-school student-on-student harassment claims, and verified all fingerprints. Checked archived "as hereinafter defined" phrasing in subsection 1 (definition resides in section 213.010) and nonpublic club/religious exemptions with public-patron carve-out in subsection 3. All 3 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Aiding, retaliation, government, and association discrimination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (4)) and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43). Lists unlawful practices including aiding/abetting/coercing chapter violations, retaliation for opposition or participation, discrimination by the state or political subdivisions (note grammatical structure inside subdivision (3) under the subsection 1 lead-in), and discrimination based on association with protected persons. Separate review: Revised during review from "Aiding, retaliation, government discrimination, and association claims" because subsection 1 defines unlawful discriminatory practices rather than procedural claims.

headings.title: Exclusive employment-claim remedy with chapters 285 and 287
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. States that chapter 213, together with chapters 285 and 287, provides the exclusive remedy for claims for injury or damages arising out of an employment relationship. Separate review: Revised during review from "Exclusive remedy for employment-relationship claims" to preserve the exact statutory cross-references to chapters 285 and 287 rather than suggesting chapter 213 alone is exclusive.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including subsection 1 subdivisions (1) to (4)) and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43) and verified all fingerprints. Checked lead-in coverage, subdivision (3) state/political-subdivision syntax, and chapters 285 and 287 reference in subsection 2. Revised subsection 1 title from "claims" to "discrimination" and subsection 2 title to name chapters 285 and 287 explicitly.

headings.title: Verified complaint, 180-day filing limit, and jurisdictional defense
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1986 S.B. 513 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43), including the 2000 Foster v. BJC Health System annotation (121 F.Supp.2d 1280) on termination-notice accrual. Covers verified written complaints within 180 days as a jurisdictional condition precedent, filing by agent/attorney/attorney general, mandatory jurisdictional determination, dismissal of untimely complaints, and asserting untimeliness as a complete defense at any time.

headings.title: Deemed filing and seven-day forwarding with federal and local agencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Treats complaints filed with the EEOC, work-sharing/deferral federal agencies, or certified local commissions as filed with the commission on receipt, provides reciprocal deemed filing for local commissions, and sets seven-day copy-forwarding duties.

headings.title: Investigation, probable cause determination, and conciliation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs the executive director and staff to promptly investigate complaints, endeavor to eliminate practices by conference, conciliation, and persuasion upon finding probable cause, and report results under commission rules and guidelines.

headings.title: Joining additional or substitute respondents during investigation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Permits joining an unnamed person identified during investigation as an additional or substitute respondent upon written notice stating the reason for joinder in accordance with commission rules.

headings.title: Notice of hearing, hearing body, and venue
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Authorizes the chairperson, if conciliation fails and circumstances warrant, to issue and serve hearing notices before a three-member commission panel or licensed-attorney hearing examiner, with respondent's written option to locate the hearing in the county of residence or business.

headings.title: Applicability of hearing procedures absent circuit court election
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Applies the statutory hearing procedures where written notice of hearing has been issued and no party has elected circuit court under section 213.076.

headings.title: Commission counsel, investigator separation, and conciliation exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and notes. Makes the commission a party represented by the attorney general or delegated staff attorney, bars investigators from serving as panel members or hearing examiners, and excludes evidence of conciliation endeavors.

headings.title: Answers, complainant intervention, amendments, and transcribed oath testimony
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and notes. Covers respondent's verified answer and appearance, discretionary complainant intervention (with party status for discovery and depositions), reasonable amendments to complaints and answers, and transcribed testimony under oath.

headings.title: Discovery rights and sanctions in contested cases
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and notes. Authorizes civil-procedure discovery methods in contested commission cases and empowers the panel or hearing examiner to impose sanctions under the rules of civil procedure.

headings.title: Conduct of hearings under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and notes. Directs that the administrative hearing be conducted in the manner provided by chapter 536.

headings.title: Panel hearings, remedial orders, and tiered civil penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 (including subdivisions (1) and (2), paragraphs (a) to (c), and continuation paragraph) and notes. Covers chairperson selection of the panel and presiding officer, presiding officer powers, findings and conclusions, cease-and-desist and affirmative-action orders, tiered civil penalties up to $2,000/$5,000/$10,000 for specified housing and related section 213.070 violations, and deposit of civil penalties into the human rights fund.

headings.title: Panel findings of no violation and dismissal orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and notes. Distinguished from subsection 11 by requiring written findings, conclusions, and an order dismissing the complaint served on complainant and respondent when no unlawful discriminatory practice is found.

headings.title: Hearing examiner powers, findings, and recommended orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and notes. Grants hearing examiners the powers of section 213.030(8) and subsection 11 and requires findings of fact, conclusions of law, and a recommended order for subsection 11 relief or subsection 12 dismissal.

headings.title: Panel review of examiner recommendations and order service
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and notes. Requires a three-member commission panel to review the examiner's record, findings, and recommended order, accept or amend it as the commission's order, serve orders on parties, and deliver copies to the attorney general and appropriate public officers.

headings.title: Protection of prior bona fide real estate transactions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 15 and notes. Prevents commission orders under section 213.075 from affecting contracts, sales, encumbrances, or leases consummated before the order with a bona fide purchaser lacking actual notice of the charge.

headings.title: Appeals of commission orders under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 16 and notes. Provides that any person aggrieved by a commission order may appeal as provided in chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 16 subsections (including subsection 11 subdivisions (1)–(2), paragraphs (a)–(c), and continuation paragraph) and all notes (L. 1986 S.B. 513 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43), including the 2000 Foster v. BJC Health System annotation (121 F.Supp.2d 1280) on notice of termination starting the filing period, and verified all fingerprints. Checked 180-day jurisdictional defense, EEOC/local agency deemed filing and 7-day forwarding, joinder, section 213.076 circuit-court election, discovery/sanctions, chapter 536 hearings/appeals, panel vs. hearing examiner orders, tiered civil penalties to the human rights fund, and bona fide real estate transaction protection. All 16 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Election of civil action for specified housing-related notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1619). Allows a complainant or respondent to elect a civil action in lieu of a section 213.075 hearing within twenty days of mailing of a hearing notice alleging violations of sections 213.040, 213.045, 213.050, or related section 213.070 violations including aiding and abetting.

headings.title: Commencement by commission staff attorneys and claimant expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the chairperson to have commission staff attorneys commence and maintain a civil action on the complainant's behalf within thirty days of election, with claimant expenses paid by the commission.

headings.title: Intervention as of right by aggrieved persons
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Grants any person aggrieved with respect to the issues in a civil action under this section the right to intervene.

headings.title: Available section 213.111 relief and nonparty discovery bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes courts to grant section 213.111 relief upon finding an unlawful practice occurred or is about to occur, while barring monetary relief for a nonparty aggrieved person who fails to comply with court discovery orders.

headings.title: Commission authority to hire attorneys
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Authorizes the commission to hire attorneys necessary to carry out its duties under section 213.076.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1619) and verified all fingerprints. Checked 20-day circuit-court election for sections 213.040/213.045/213.050 and related 213.070 notices, 30-day commencement by staff attorneys with commission-paid claimant expenses, intervention as of right, section 213.111 relief with nonparty discovery-noncompliance bar, and attorney hiring authority. All 5 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Settlement and conciliation efforts, approval, and confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1619). Directs settlement and conciliation to the extent feasible between complaint filing and charge, hearing setting, or dismissal, subjects agreements to executive director approval, and restricts public disclosure or evidentiary use without both parties' written consent.

headings.title: Record access for employment and public-accommodation complaints
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1) to (8)) and history note. Governs public and party access to investigative records, closure documents, and settlement/conciliation agreements for section 213.055, 213.065, and 213.070 employment and public-accommodation complaints, with an interagency-sharing exception. Retained verbatim source wording in subdivision (2) ('under section 213.111 for a right to or other legal proceedings') without silently inserting 'sue'.

headings.title: Record access and agreement disclosure for housing-related complaints
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note. Applies subdivisions (1), (2), (4), (5), (7), and (8) of subsection 2 to complaints under sections 213.040, 213.045, 213.050, or related section 213.070 provisions, and makes settlement or conciliation agreements public unless the parties agree otherwise and the executive director determines disclosure is not required.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections (including subsection 2 subdivisions (1) to (8) and subsection 3 subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1619) and verified all fingerprints. Checked executive director approval and confidentiality in subsection 1, employment/public-accommodation vs. housing record-access distinctions, and verified verbatim source omission in subsection 2(2) ("under section 213.111 for a right to or other legal proceedings", missing "sue") is retained without silent correction. All 3 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Written decisions, agreements, rules, and copies to parties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513, A.L. 1992 H.B. 1619). Requires final decisions, settlement and conciliation agreements, findings, rules, and orders of the commission to be in writing and requires sending copies of decisions and orders to parties.

headings.title: Thirty-day deadline to petition for judicial review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Allows any aggrieved person to seek circuit court judicial review of a final commission decision, finding, rule, or order within thirty days after mailing or delivery of notice.

headings.title: Chapter 536 review procedures and venue options
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Specifies judicial review under chapter 536 and lets the appealing party choose venue in Cole County or the county of residence or a corporation's registered or business office.

headings.title: Commission enforcement petitions, record, and scope of inquiry
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes the commission to seek circuit court enforcement if no timely review proceeding is filed, specifies venue and certified-record contents (noting archived wording 'prescribed by this action'), and limits court inquiry to statutory authority/jurisdiction and substantial compliance.

headings.title: Private enforcement petitions after sixty days
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Allows a person entitled to relief to petition for circuit court enforcement sixty days after the order if neither judicial review nor a commission enforcement petition is filed, incorporating subsection 4's petition contents and jurisdiction. Preserves source cross-reference 'within the time established under subsection 3 of this section' without altering it, though the 30-day period appears in subsection 2.

headings.title: Enforcement orders and four affirmative defenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 (subdivisions (1) to (4)) and history note. Requires the circuit court in a subsection 4 or 5 enforcement suit to enforce the commission decision unless the resisting party affirmatively proves lack of court jurisdiction/venue, constitutional violation, commission action beyond authority/jurisdiction, or substantial compliance. Separate review: Revised during review from "Mandatory enforcement order and four affirmative defenses" to avoid characterizing an order conditioned on the absence of four affirmative defenses as unconditionally mandatory.

headings.title: Actions for breach of settlement or conciliation agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (noting official catchline spells 'breach' as 'breech' while subsection 7 uses 'breach'). Directs the commission to file circuit court actions upon deeming a breach of a settlement or conciliation agreement, while preserving parties' right to sue personally.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 7 subsections (including subsection 6 subdivisions (1) to (4)) and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513, A.L. 1992 H.B. 1619) and verified all fingerprints. Checked official catchline spelling ("breech" vs. "breach" in subsection 7), archived subsection 4 wording ("prescribed by this action"), and verified source cross-reference discrepancy in subsection 5 ("within the time established under subsection 3 of this section", though the 30-day deadline appears in subsection 2) is documented and retained without alteration. Revised subsection 6 title to remove "Mandatory" for an order subject to four affirmative defenses; retained other 6 titles.

headings.title: Statutory construction and nonrepeal of other antidiscrimination laws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513 § 213.100 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43). Directs construction of chapter 213 to accomplish its purposes, overrides inconsistent laws, and states chapter 213 does not repeal other state antidiscrimination laws.

headings.title: Abrogation of McBryde and required business judgment instruction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Expressly abrogates McBryde v. Ritenour School District (207 S.W.3d 162) and its progeny on business judgment instructions and requires giving a business judgment rule instruction to juries in chapter 213 civil actions.

headings.title: McDonnell Douglas analysis for employer Rule 74.04 motions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs courts considering employer motions under Missouri Rule of Civil Procedure 74.04 in cases without direct evidence of discrimination to treat the McDonnell Douglas Corp. v. Green (411 U.S. 792) burden-shifting analysis as highly persuasive. Separate review: Revised during review from "McDonnell Douglas analysis for Rule 74.04 summary judgment motions" to identify accurately that the rule applies specifically to employer motions under Rule 74.04 in non-direct-evidence cases.

headings.title: Abrogation of Daugherty contributing-factor standard
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Expressly abrogates Daugherty v. City of Maryland Heights (231 S.W.3d 814) and its progeny regarding the contributing-factor standard and abandonment of the McDonnell Douglas burden-shifting framework.

headings.title: Abrogation of Hurst and Thomas causation instruction holdings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Expressly abrogates Hurst v. Kansas City Mo. School District (437 S.W.3d 327) on applying MAI 19.01 to chapter 213 actions and Thomas v. McKeever's Enterprises, Inc. (388 S.W.3d 206) on barring 'but for' causation instructions.

headings.title: Abrogation of pre-August 28, 2017 chapter jury instructions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Abrogates all Missouri-approved jury instructions specifically addressing chapter 213 civil actions that were in effect prior to August 28, 2017.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 6 subsections and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513 § 213.100 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43) and verified all fingerprints. Checked statutory construction/nonrepeal rule, express abrogations of McBryde, Daugherty, Hurst, Thomas, and pre-August 28, 2017 chapter 213 MAI instructions, business judgment instruction mandate, and employer Rule 74.04 McDonnell Douglas standard. Revised subsection 3 title to specify employer Rule 74.04 motions; retained other 5 titles.

headings.title: Right-to-sue notices, venue, termination, and filing deadlines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and all notes (L. 1986 S.B. 513 § 213.110 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43), including footnote * noting 'of subsection 1' did not appear in original rolls (after S.B. 43 added subsections to 213.070) and the 1998 Whitmore annotation (156 F.3d 796). Covers written-request right-to-sue letters (after 180 days for employment/public-accommodation complaints or upon request for housing complaints), sole issuance conditions, circuit or associate circuit venue, termination of commission proceedings, bar on refiling, and 90-day and two-year court filing limits.

headings.title: Injunctive relief, damages, costs, and attorney fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes, including the 1999 Kline annotation (175 F.3d 660) on punitive damages against municipalities. Authorizes injunctions, restraining orders, actual and punitive damages, and discretionary court costs and reasonable attorney fees to prevailing parties other than state or local commissions, limiting prevailing-respondent attorney fees to cases without foundation.

headings.title: Right to trial by jury
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes, including the 2003 State ex rel. Diehl v. O'Malley annotation (95 S.W.3d 82). Grants any party to an action initiated under section 213.111 a right to a jury trial.

headings.title: Caps on combined actual and punitive damages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (subdivisions (1) and (2), paragraphs (a) to (d)) and notes. Caps each complaining party's combined actual (including nonpecuniary) and punitive damages at actual back pay plus interest and tiered respondent-size limits ($50,000; $100,000; $200,000; or $500,000 based on employee counts across 20 or more calendar weeks).

headings.title: Plaintiff's burden of proof in employment-related civil actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Places the burden on plaintiffs in employment-related civil actions under chapter 213 to prove the alleged unlawful decision or action was taken because of protected classification and was the direct proximate cause of claimed damages.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections (including subsection 4 subdivisions (1)–(2) and paragraphs (a)–(d)) and all notes (L. 1986 S.B. 513 § 213.110 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 43), including footnote * ("of subsection 1" added by Revisor after S.B. 43 added subsections to 213.070) and the 1998 Whitmore (156 F.3d 796), 1999 Kline (175 F.3d 660), and 2003 State ex rel. Diehl v. O'Malley (95 S.W.3d 82) annotations, and verified all fingerprints. Checked 180-day/immediate right-to-sue rules, 90-day and 2-year filing limits, remedies and prevailing-respondent fee standard, jury trial right, employee-size damages caps, and employment causation burden. All 5 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Attorney general actions for pattern, practice, or public-importance denials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513 § 213.125, A.L. 1992 H.B. 1619). Authorizes the attorney general, upon reasonable cause to believe there is a pattern or practice of resistance or a group denial raising an issue of general public importance, to sue in state court for preventive injunctive or other relief.

headings.title: Chairperson-authorized actions for temporary or preliminary relief
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Allows the chairperson, after a complaint under sections 213.040 to 213.070 is filed and prompt judicial action is deemed necessary, to authorize the attorney general to seek temporary or preliminary equitable relief in circuit court.

headings.title: Circuit court enforcement of commission subpoenas
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs the attorney general, upon request by the commission, to take appropriate action in circuit court to enforce a commission-issued subpoena.

headings.title: Suits to enforce referred agreements or commission orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes the attorney general to file suit to enforce a settlement agreement, conciliation agreement, or commission order referred by the commission or executive director.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and history note (L. 1986 S.B. 513 § 213.125, A.L. 1992 H.B. 1619) and verified all fingerprints. Checked pattern-or-practice/public-importance attorney general suits, chairperson-authorized temporary/preliminary equitable relief actions, mandatory subpoena enforcement upon commission request, and permissive enforcement suits for referred agreements or orders. All 4 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Substantial-equivalency certification prerequisite for local commissions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1619). Prohibits municipal or county commissions from hearing chapter 213 complaints unless certified as substantially equivalent by the state commission based on substantially similar procedural protections in the establishing ordinance.

headings.title: Five-year reviews, deficiency negotiations, and decertification appeals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires commission review of each local commission's certification at least every five years, directs staff negotiations to correct deficiencies in protecting procedural or substantive rights, and allows chapter 536 circuit court appeals of decertification decisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1619) and verified all fingerprints. Checked substantial-equivalency certification prerequisite for municipal/county commissions, five-year review cycle, staff deficiency negotiations, and chapter 536 circuit court decertification appeals. Both titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Certified local commission jurisdiction, state exclusion, and hearing powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1619). Empowers certified section 213.020(3) local commissions to hear complaints of local chapter 213 violations and exercise hearing, subpoena, oath, testimony, and document-production powers consistent with chapter 213, while barring complaints against the state of Missouri, the University of Missouri system, or their officers, agencies, or employees.

headings.title: Empowerment by local legislative bodies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Allows the legislative body of the city, town, village, or county served by a section 213.020(3) local commission to empower it to exercise section 213.135 powers notwithstanding contrary law, charter, or ordinance.

headings.title: Local proceedings under section 213.075, local counsel, and recording
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires local proceedings to follow section 213.075, substituting local government counsel for the attorney general, providing for hearing-examiner proposals or orders as allowed by ordinance, and requiring tape recording or a certified court reporter.

headings.title: Commission examiner review, record transmission, finality, and appeal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Delays appeal finality of local orders pending commission hearing-examiner review, sets 30-day order filing, 15-day transcript/exhibit transmission, and 90-day opinion deadlines, and governs finality and appeals under section 213.085.

headings.title: Circuit court enforcement of unappealed local orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Allows filing a circuit court enforcement petition as provided in section 213.085 if no appeal from a final local commission order is filed within thirty days.

headings.title: Adoption and state commission approval of local procedural rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Permits local commissions to adopt chapter-consistent procedural rules for investigations, conciliation, and hearings, conditioned on Missouri Commission on Human Rights review and approval (including adoption of commission amendments).

All 6 titles retained as accurate.
